what_it_does: Training large language models on very long documents requires splitting each document across multiple GPUs — a technique called sequence parallelism — so that no single GPU has to hold an entire very long context in memory. Existing sequence-parallel approaches assume all documents in a training batch are roughly the same length and split them evenly across GPUs. Real training data, however, has a highly uneven distribution: most documents are short, but a small number are extremely long. With a fixed even-split strategy, GPUs assigned to short documents finish early and sit idle while the GPUs assigned to the long outlier documents are still working, wasting capacity. FlexSP adapts the splitting strategy per document: a short document might be handled by just one GPU while a very long document is spread across many, with the degree of splitting chosen dynamically each batch to keep all GPUs busy. The communication and attention computation (the main per-token dot-product operation in transformers) are co-designed to work efficiently under this variable splitting.
